The Osun State Police Command has confirmed the deaths of two persons in separate attacks involving suspected rival cult groups that occurred between Thursday and Saturday in Ilesa, Osun State. But sources in the Isokun area of Ilesa, where the first killing occurred, told our correspondent on Sunday, on condition of anonymity for security reasons, that two men were killed there. They identified the deceased as Bobo and White. They said the duo were suspected members of the Eiye confraternity, adding that the assailants rode on a motorcycle and arrived at the scene around 9:45pm on Thursday. A resident, identified as Titi, said in a telephone interview with PUNCH Metro on Sunday that the assailants shot the deceased in the head and injured one other man. The deceased are popularly known as Bobo and White. Both are members of the Eiye Confraternity, and the other guy in critical condition does not belong to any cult group. “Before the attackers arrived, there was a misunderstanding among some people around Alafin’s joint. Suddenly, some people came on a motorcycle and took advantage of the situation on the ground and hit their targets at close range. They shot the deceased in the head. “The reason behind this attack is not clear. While some people said old rifts between the Eiye and KK confraternity in the town were the cause, some said it is politically motivated because the father of one of the two men killed is a serving councillor in one of the wards in Ilesa West,” Titi said. 2027: PDP inaugurates 22-member committee for Osun senator’s re-election Mob kills Osun accident survivor, police hunt suspects Mob kills accident survivor after crash claims two lives in Osun In the second attack, two individuals identified as P. A and Omo Mummy were allegedly shot around Omi-Eran Atijo, in Ilesa, around 8:15pm on Saturday. It was, however, learnt that one of them later died as a result of injuries sustained in the attack. A source close to the scene said those who carried out the attack shot the duo at close range before fleeing the area. The cause of the current rift could not be immediately established, as the return of hostilities involving suspected cultists, at a time when normalcy was gradually returning to different parts of the state ravaged by extrajudicial killings before the last August 15 governorship poll, has continued to raise concerns in security circles. When contacted for confirmation, the Osun State Police Command Public Relations Officer, Abiodun Ojelabi, said one person each was killed in the Isokun and Omi-Eran incidents, blaming the development on rival cult groups. “In the Isokun incident, one person was killed, not two. In the Omi-Eran incident, one life was also lost. Police operatives were informed about the incident at Omi-Eran around 7:10am this morning. Maybe it happened earlier. “We have mobilised to the area. Normalcy has returned, and we are going after the perpetrators. The killings are cult-related,” Ojelabi said. Kindly share this story:
